title: The Perpetual Virginity of Mary
summary: The Blessed Virgin Mary remained a virgin before, during, and after the birth of Christ (ante partum, in partu, et post partum), a dogma defined by the Lateran Council (649) and reaffirmed by Trent and Vatican II, signifying her total consecration to God and the divine origin of the Incarnation.

blocks.text: Introduction: The Threefold Virginity

The Church confesses that Mary realized in her person and life a unique holiness: she remained a virgin before the birth of Christ, during his birth, and after his birth. This threefold virginity—ante partum, in partu, et post partum—is a dogma of the Catholic faith, not merely a pious opinion. [CCC 499-501]

This doctrine safeguards the divine origin of the Incarnation and Mary's total consecration to God's plan. Mary's virginity is not a denial of the goodness of marriage but a sign that the Incarnation is entirely God's work, initiated by the Holy Spirit, not human power. [CCC 503, 505]
Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel (which means, God with us).

blocks.title: CCC 499-501: Threefold Virginity
blocks.text: Mary remained a virgin before, during, and after Christ's birth; this threefold virginity is a dogma signifying her total consecration and the divine origin of the Incarnation.
I. Virginity Before the Birth of Christ (Ante Partum)

Mary conceived Jesus by the power of the Holy Spirit without any human intervention. The angel Gabriel announced this virginal conception, and Mary asked how this could be since she knew no man. The Holy Spirit overshadowed her, and the power of the Most High conceived the Son of God in her womb. [CCC 488, 496]

This virginal conception fulfills the prophecy of Isaiah: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son. The Creed confesses that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary. This affirms that God alone is the Father of Jesus in his divinity, and the Incarnation is entirely God's initiative. [CCC 488, 496]

And Mary said to the angel, How shall this be, since I have no husband? And the angel said to her, The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.

blocks.title: CCC 488: Virginal Conception
blocks.text: Mary conceived by the Holy Spirit without human intervention, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy; this affirms God alone is Father of Jesus and the Incarnation is God's initiative.
II. Virginity During the Birth of Christ (In Partu)

The Church teaches that Mary's virginity was not violated during the birth of Christ. The birth was miraculous and painless, without injury to Mary's virginal integrity. This is symbolized in liturgical art by the closed gate of Ezekiel's vision, through which only the Lord may pass. [CCC 499]

The Fathers of the Church compared Mary's womb to a sealed garden, a fountain sealed, through which only Christ passed. This mystery signifies that Christ's birth did not diminish but consecrated his mother's virginity. The divine infant came forth from her womb as light passes through glass, without breaking it. [CCC 499]
And the LORD said to me: This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it; therefore it shall remain shut.

blocks.title: CCC 499: Virginal Birth
blocks.text: Mary's virginity was not violated during Christ's birth; the birth was miraculous and painless, symbolized by Ezekiel's closed gate through which only the Lord passed.
III. Virginity After the Birth of Christ (Post Partum)

Mary remained a virgin after the birth of Christ, never having marital relations with Joseph or bearing other children. The perpetual virginity after childbirth has been constantly taught by the Church's magisterium and is defined dogma. Mary and Joseph lived in a virginal marriage, with Joseph as the guardian of Mary's virginity. [CCC 500, 506]

The brethren of Jesus mentioned in Scripture are understood as close relatives (cousins or step-brothers from Joseph's previous marriage, according to some traditions), not children of Mary. The Church has always interpreted these passages in light of the dogma of perpetual virginity. [CCC 500]
When Joseph woke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took his wife, but knew her not until she had borne a son; and he called his name Jesus.

blocks.title: CCC 500: Perpetual Virginity
blocks.text: Mary remained a virgin after Christ's birth, never having relations with Joseph; the brethren of Jesus are close relatives, not Mary's children, as constantly taught by the magisterium.
IV. The Lateran Council (649): Dogmatic Definition

The Lateran Council of 649, under Pope Martin I, defined the dogma of Mary's perpetual virginity with precision. The Council anathematized anyone who does not properly and truly confess that the holy and ever-Virgin Mary is the Mother of God, remaining a virgin before, during, and after the birth. [Lateran Council 649]

This Council clarified what the Church had always believed, responding to those who denied Mary's virginity after childbirth. The definition safeguards the uniqueness of Christ's birth and Mary's total consecration to God's plan of salvation. [CCC 499-501]
And she gave birth to her first-born son and wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.

blocks.title: Lateran Council (649): Defined Dogma
blocks.text: The Lateran Council defined that Mary remained a virgin before, during, and after birth, anathematizing deniers; this safeguards Christ's unique birth and Mary's total consecration.
V. The Magisterium: Trent and Vatican II

The Council of Trent (1545-1563) reaffirmed the perpetual virginity of Mary against Protestant denials. Trent taught that Mary is ever-Virgin and that this doctrine is to be held by all the faithful. The Council anathematized those who denied this truth. [Trent Session XXV]

Vatican Council II (1962-1965) reaffirmed this dogma in Lumen Gentium, teaching that Mary is the ever-Virgin Mother of God. The Council emphasized that this virginity signifies Mary's total gift of self to God and her unique role in the economy of salvation. [Lumen Gentium 52, 57]
For he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden. For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.

blocks.title: Trent & Vatican II: Ever-Virgin
blocks.text: Trent reaffirmed Mary's perpetual virginity against Protestant denials; Vatican II taught she is ever-Virgin, signifying her total gift of self to God and unique salvific role.
VI. Theological Significance of Perpetual Virginity

Mary's perpetual virginity signifies that Jesus has God alone as his Father in his divinity. The virginal conception and birth reveal that the Incarnation is entirely God's work, not initiated by human desire or power. Salvation comes from the Lord, not from human effort. [CCC 503, 505]

Mary's virginity also signifies her total and undivided consecration to God's will. She is the model of the Church's virginity, faith, and charity. Her virginity is a sign of eschatological life, pointing to the resurrection when there will be neither marrying nor giving in marriage. [CCC 506, 972]
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

blocks.title: CCC 503, 506: Sign of Divine Initiative
blocks.text: Mary's virginity signifies that Jesus has God alone as Father and the Incarnation is God's work; it also signifies her total consecration and points to eschatological life.
VII. Mary as Model of Virginity and Consecration

Mary is the model and mother of all who consecrate their virginity to God. Consecrated virgins, religious, and all the faithful look to Mary as the exemplar of total dedication to Christ. Her virginity is a sign of the Church's spousal love for Christ. [CCC 972]

The Church teaches that virginity or celibacy for the sake of the Kingdom is a superior state to marriage, not because marriage is evil, but because virginity signifies undivided devotion to the Lord. Mary exemplifies this total gift of self to God's plan. [CCC 1618-1620]
I want you to be free from anxieties. The unmarried man is anxious about the affairs of the Lord, how to please the Lord; but the married man is anxious about worldly affairs, how to please his wife.

blocks.title: CCC 972: Model for Consecrated Life
blocks.text: Mary is the model for all who consecrate virginity to God; her virginity signifies the Church's spousal love for Christ and undivided devotion to the Lord.
VIII. Objections and Responses

Some object that Scripture mentions the brethren of Jesus, implying Mary had other children. The Church interprets these as close relatives, noting that the term brethren in Semitic usage includes cousins and other kin. The context of Scripture and Tradition supports perpetual virginity. [CCC 500]

Others claim that perpetual virginity denies the goodness of marriage. The Church responds that virginity is not a rejection of marriage's goodness but a higher calling for the sake of the Kingdom. Mary's virginal marriage with Joseph shows that marriage can be holy without sexual relations. [CCC 506]
When Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing near, he said to his mother, Woman, behold, your son! Then he said to the disciple, Behold, your mother!

blocks.title: CCC 500: Brethren of Jesus
blocks.text: The brethren of Jesus are close relatives, not Mary's children; Semitic usage includes cousins as brethren, and Scripture and Tradition support perpetual virginity.
IX. Joseph's Role as Guardian of Virginity

St. Joseph is the chaste spouse of Mary and the guardian of her virginity. He is the foster father of Jesus, protecting and providing for the Holy Family while respecting Mary's consecration to God. Joseph's chastity is a model for all husbands and fathers. [CCC 506]

The marriage of Mary and Joseph was a true marriage, though virginal. It fulfilled all the essential properties of marriage except sexual union, which was not necessary because the child was conceived by the Holy Spirit. Their marriage shows that love is not dependent on physical intimacy. [CCC 506]

But as he considered this, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

blocks.title: CCC 506: Chaste Spouse
blocks.text: Joseph is the chaste spouse and guardian of Mary's virginity; their virginal marriage was true marriage, showing love is not dependent on physical intimacy.
X. The Immaculate Conception and Virginity

Mary's perpetual virginity is connected to her Immaculate Conception. Preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception, Mary was filled with grace and free from all disordered desires. This purity enabled her to consecrate her virginity totally to God. [CCC 490-493]

Pope Pius IX, in Ineffabilis Deus (1854), defined the Immaculate Conception, noting that Mary was full of grace and always united to God's will. Her perpetual virginity flows from this fullness of grace and her unique holiness. [Ineffabilis Deus]
And he came to her and said, Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you!

blocks.title: CCC 490-493: Immaculate and Virgin
blocks.text: Mary's Immaculate Conception preserved her from original sin, filling her with grace; this purity enabled her total consecration of virginity to God's plan.
XI. Living the Faith in Mary's Virginity

To believe in Mary's perpetual virginity is to deepen our faith in the Incarnation and the divinity of Christ. We honor Mary by imitating her purity, consecration, and total surrender to God's will. Through her intercession, we grow in chastity and dedication to God. [CCC 506, 971]

The Church celebrates several feasts honoring Mary's virginity: the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God (January 1), the Annunciation (March 25), and the Assumption (August 15). The rosary and other Marian devotions help us meditate on this mystery and seek Mary's intercession. [CCC 971, 2676]
Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God? You are not your own; you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

blocks.title: CCC 506: Imitate Mary's Purity
blocks.text: Belief in Mary's virginity deepens faith in the Incarnation; we honor her by imitating her purity and consecration, seeking her intercession for chastity and dedication to God.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer: Memorare
blocks.text: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection, implored thy help, or sought thine intercession was left unaided. Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my Mother. To thee do I come, before thee I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in thy mercy hear and answer me. Amen.
